chunks: Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurara ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying that the charity (Zakat) is not permissible for the professional, nor for the one with capability, normal, strong, so let them keep themselves away from it.

key_terms.لِمُحْتَرِفٍ: The professional (one with a steady trade or job)

ai.seo_question: Who is eligible to receive Zakat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) clarifies that Zakat is prohibited for the 'muhtarif' (those engaged in trade or business) and the 'dhul mirrah sawiyy' (the able-bodied and healthy), as they possess the capacity to earn their livelihood. This hadith, recorded in Al-Kafi, underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on Zakat as a purifying charity for the destitute rather than a general welfare subsidy for the self-sufficient, ensuring resources reach those truly in need.

en.hubeali:
Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz Bin Abdullah, from Zurara Bin Ayn, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I heard himasws saying that the charity (Zakāt) is not Permissible for the professional, nor for the one with capability, normal, strong, so he should keep himself away from it (taking the Zakāt)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Hammad ibn ‘Isa has narrated from Hariz ibn ‘Abd Allah from Zurarah ibn ’A‘yan who has said the following: “I once heard abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
Charity (Zakat) is not lawful for those who have an established profession or a resourceful one who is capable and strong, so keep yourselves clean from receiving charity (Zakat).”’
